body.statement: If \(P\) is homogeneous of degree \(r\geq1\) and \(\det G_P\equiv0\) in \(\mathbb R[S3]\), then symmetry of the second derivative gives \(\mathrm dG_{P,X}\{Q_P(X)\}=0\). Consequently \(Q_P\{\mathcal T_P(X,t)\}=Q_P(X)\) and \(P\{\mathcal T_P(X,t)\}=P(X)\) for every \(X\in S3\) and \(t\in\mathbb R\).
body.justification: This converts determinant singularity and symmetric-gradient integrability into exact finite translation invariance under the trace-pairing convention.
body.gap: De Bondt supplies a quasi-translation criterion, but does not derive the adjugate direction from a symmetric gradient or combine it with positive-cone order.
body.consumer: Theorem 2 transports a rank-two null direction along exact polynomial rays.
